newsitem.title: USA: Berger argues against revoking MFN for China.
newsitem.headline: Berger argues against revoking MFN for China.

text.p: White House National Security Adviser Sandy Berger warned Congress on Friday that revoking Most Favoured Nation trade status for China could "destroy the dialogue" between Washington and Beijing.

In remarks prepared for delivery Friday night, Berger said a vote by Congress to revoke the favourable tariff treatment for Chinese goods entering the United States would weaken Hong Kong, do "grievous injury" to U.S. interests and "cut off our contact with the Chinese people," rather than strengthening the forces for human rights.

"In laying out the purpose of our strategic dialogue with China and the propositions behind it, I want to end with one development that could destroy the dialogue, do grievous injury to the interests of the United States and shatter a new consensus on China -- a vote by Congress to revoke Most Favored Nation trade status for China," Berger said.

President Bill Clinton has decided to extend MFN to China for another year but some members of Congress are opposed because of concerns about Chinese human rights practices, allegations that Beijing is contributing to the spread of weapons of mass destruction and worry about the future of Hong Kong when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.

"Revoking MFN would make China more isolated and less likely to play by the rules of international conduct," Berger said in the speech prepared for delivery to the Council of Foreign Relations in New York.
"Treating China as our enemy could well make China our enemy," he said.
